questions.explain: The three AI bottlenecks: vector-search CPU (dm_exec_query_stats — avg_cpu_ms climbing means the index needs attention), connection pressure (dm_os_waiting_tasks — THREADPOOL means pool exhaustion), and hot-row blocking (dm_exec_requests blocking_session_id).
options: Watch vector-search CPU via query stats, connection pressure via waiting tasks, and hot-row blocking via exec requests
DMVs are not useful for AI workloads
questions.q: Which DMVs matter most for AI workload health?

questions.explain: Text-to-SQL and agent tools generate queries the DBA never wrote — Query Store captures every distinct query text with plans and runtime stats automatically, enabling regression detection and plan forcing while the AI layer is fixed.
options: Query Store is irrelevant for AI apps
Only use it for manual queries
Query Store is the safety net for generated SQL — automatic plan history, regression detection, and plan forcing
questions.q: Why is Query Store especially important for AI applications?

questions.explain: Join the halves with shared keys: time (created_at on both sides), query text hash (stored in agent_actions, joined to Query Store), and tenant_id (audit rows + Resource Governor tagging) — one incident runbook across both.
options: The two halves cannot be correlated
Correlate with shared keys: time, generated-SQL query hash, and tenant_id — one incident runbook across both halves
